messages.content: The organizer moved the first Minneapolis meeting to 8:45 Thursday morning, so I’m ruling out the same-day flight. Compare Wednesday evening flights and one downtown hotel night. The hotel reimbursement limit is $300 including tax, and I still need a Thursday flight leaving after 4:00 p.m.

Understood. I’ll compare the Wednesday evening options using total trip cost, arrival practicality, hotel walking time to the downtown office, and cancellation terms. For Thursday, do you want only the existing 6:20 p.m. return considered, or should I include an earlier departure after 4:00 p.m.?
Include an earlier one. The ending time still isn’t confirmed, so don’t narrow it to a single return yet.

There are two useful nonstop return choices: 4:35-6:07 p.m. for a higher fare, and the existing 6:20-7:52 p.m. flight. I’ll keep both in the comparison. How late can you reasonably leave Chicago Wednesday?
I can leave the office around 4:30. I don’t want a departure before 6:30 because getting to O’Hare would be tight.

That leaves two practical nonstop outbound flights:

• 7:10-8:42 p.m., the flight already identified.
• 8:25-9:57 p.m., which is cheaper but puts you downtown around 10:40 p.m. under normal traffic.

The 7:10 departure provides less margin from your office but should still be workable if you leave at 4:30. The 8:25 is safer operationally, though it makes for a shorter night before the 8:45 meeting.
What are the fares when paired with each return?

Current round-trip totals are:

• 7:10 Wednesday outbound + 4:35 Thursday return: $368.
• 7:10 outbound + 6:20 return: $329.
• 8:25 Wednesday outbound + 4:35 Thursday return: $346.
• 8:25 outbound + 6:20 return: $307.

All four are nonstop economy itineraries. The fares permit changes before departure, but any fare difference applies; cancellation produces a carrier credit rather than a cash refund.
Now the hotels. Keep it genuinely walkable to the office, not something that only looks close on a map.

The two strongest options within the reimbursement amount are:

Hampton Inn & Suites Downtown: $246.80 including tax. It is about a seven-minute walk to the office using normal street crossings. Breakfast is included. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. Tuesday, May 12; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax.

Hyatt Place Downtown: $287.40 including tax. It is about a four-minute walk with a simpler route and no long avenue crossing. Cancellation is free until 11:59 p.m. Monday, May 11; after that, the full one-night charge applies.

Both have rooms available for Wednesday, May 13, and both are below the $300 reimbursable limit.
How much should I allow for the airport transfers?

Using current weekday estimates, allow about $36 for a rideshare from MSP to either hotel Wednesday night and $31 from downtown back to MSP Thursday. That makes $67 in ground transportation. The light-rail alternative would cost much less, but after a late arrival it adds walking and roughly 20 to 30 minutes compared with a direct ride.
Use the rideshare estimate. Show me the best complete combination for each return time, but don’t automatically pick the cheapest outbound if the arrival is awkward.

For the 4:35 p.m. return, the best balanced combination is the 7:10 p.m. Wednesday outbound with the Hampton:

Flights: $368
Hotel: $246.80
Estimated rideshares: $67
Total: $681.80

You should reach the hotel around 9:25 to 9:40 p.m., and the office is a realistic seven-minute walk Thursday morning. This gives you the earlier trip home, but it only works if the review ends with enough time to leave downtown around 2:45 p.m.

For the 6:20 p.m. return, the same outbound and hotel produce:

Flights: $329
Hotel: $246.80
Estimated rideshares: $67
Total: $642.80

Arrival and morning logistics are identical, while the later return gives substantially more room for a delayed meeting.
So the later return saves $39. Does the Hyatt add anything useful besides three minutes of walking?

Mostly convenience rather than a material trip advantage. Its route to the office is slightly simpler, and its rooms are generally larger, but it costs $40.60 more and has the earlier cancellation deadline. For a single overnight before an early meeting, the Hampton is the stronger value unless the shorter walk is worth that premium to you.
No. Hampton is fine. I’m a little concerned about making the 7:10 departure after leaving work at 4:30. What does switching to 8:25 do to the totals?

With the Hampton and the same $67 rideshare allowance:

• 8:25 outbound + 4:35 return: $659.80 total.
• 8:25 outbound + 6:20 return: $620.80 total.

Each is $22 less than its 7:10 counterpart. The tradeoff is arrival: after landing at 9:57 p.m., baggage-free travel and a normal rideshare wait would put you at the hotel around 10:35 to 10:50 p.m.
I’ll have only a carry-on. That arrival is later than I’d like, though. Is the 7:10 realistically safe?

Leaving your office at 4:30 gives you roughly two hours and forty minutes before departure. With ordinary Wednesday traffic, that is workable and should leave a reasonable airport buffer, but a major traffic delay could reduce it quickly. The 8:25 is the safer flight to catch; the 7:10 is better for rest and still practical if you leave promptly.
Keep the 7:10. The $22 isn’t enough to justify getting downtown after 10:30. Retain both Thursday returns until the organizer confirms when we finish.

I’ve retained two complete, unbooked combinations for the Minneapolis review, both using the Wednesday 7:10-8:42 p.m. nonstop and the Hampton Inn & Suites Downtown:

Earlier return: Thursday 4:35-6:07 p.m. nonstop. Flights are $368, hotel is $246.80, estimated rideshares are $67, and projected total cost is $681.80.

Later return: Thursday 6:20-7:52 p.m. nonstop. Flights are $329, hotel is $246.80, estimated rideshares are $67, and projected total cost is $642.80.

The hotel is about a seven-minute walk from the office and can be canceled without penalty through 6:00 p.m. Tuesday, May 12. Nothing has been booked. The remaining decision is which Thursday return fits the organizer’s confirmed ending time.
